slides.say: Given: p is bigger than q, and p plus q plus r is smaller than zero. Which of the following additional givens makes r necessarily negative?

So we add one choice to the givens. Which choice makes r have to be negative? [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, starting with the choice that is easiest to check, and then ruling out the others with numbers.

[short pause] Each choice gives us another condition. We need to use it together with both givens. Where should we start? Choice number two says p is positive. That still leaves q positive, zero or negative, so there are three cases. Choice number four says q is positive. p is bigger than q, so p is positive too. That leaves only one case, so let's start there.
p and q are both positive, so p plus q is positive. But the sum of all three is negative. So r has to pull the sum down, and r must be negative.
at: p and q are both positive
r has to pull the sum down

slides.say: Let's see it in numbers. p is three and q is two, so five plus r is smaller than zero, and r is smaller than negative five. Choice number four is our answer.
at: p is three and q is two
Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to rule out the other choices with numbers. For each choice, we look for a positive r that still fits both givens and that choice. If we find one, r does not have to be negative, so that choice fails.
at: a positive r that still fits

slides.say: Choice number one, p is negative. p is negative one, q is negative two, and r is one. Negative one plus negative two plus one is negative two, smaller than zero. The givens hold, and r is positive. Out.

Choice numbers two and three. p is one, q is negative ten, and r is one. One plus negative ten plus one is negative eight. p is positive and q is negative, so both choices fit, and r is still positive. Both out. So choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: p is one, q is negative ten
